method: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from European Hematology Association, HemaSphere 'Large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL): EHA Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up' (published 23 September 2025). Every claim is a paraphrase backed by anchors (scripts/anchor.py): verify.py --source re-finds each anchored span in a fresh copy of the source, checks the claim's numbers against it and rejects copying. LICENCE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC12456099). The source's words are NOT reproduced here.

claims.claim: **Have the biopsy reported by a reference haematopathology laboratory.** Immunohistochemistry misclassifies cell of origin in up to 30% of cases, so do not withhold an active therapy on that basis alone.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association, HemaSphere, 'Large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL): EHA Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12456099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Test for MYC rearrangement by FISH, and if present test for BCL2 and BCL6,** to separate DLBCL NOS from lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 and/or BCL6 rearrangement.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association, HemaSphere, 'Large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL): EHA Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12456099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Stage with PET-CT; calculate the IPI (mandatory) and CNS-IPI (strongly advised) before treatment.** Use MRI for brain or leptomeningeal disease, add MRI and CSF analysis for patients at high CNS risk, and reserve marrow biopsy for a suspected second blood disorder.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association, HemaSphere, 'Large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL): EHA Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12456099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **An end-of-treatment PET is required for everyone.** Deauville 1–3 means complete metabolic response; because a positive scan is right only about 60% of the time, biopsy or re-scan residual uptake before acting on it.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association, HemaSphere, 'Large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL): EHA Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12456099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Stage I/II, no risk factors, non-bulky: four cycles of R-CHOP21** (IB). Up to age 80, a PET after two cycles showing complete metabolic response supports stopping at four.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association, HemaSphere, 'Large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL): EHA Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12456099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Bulky disease (largest mass 7.5 cm or more): consider six cycles of R-CHOP21** (IA).
claims.locator: European Hematology Association, HemaSphere, 'Large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL): EHA Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12456099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **One risk factor (stage III/IV, or stage I/II with poor performance status or high LDH): six cycles of R-CHOP21** (I, A). In early-stage disease, radiotherapy is usually unnecessary once six full-dose cycles achieve complete metabolic response.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association, HemaSphere, 'Large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL): EHA Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12456099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **IPI 2–5: six cycles of Pola-R-CHP are preferred** (I, B), after a 6.5% gain in 2-year PFS over R-CHOP in POLARIX; R-CHOP is an acceptable fallback. Two-weekly R-CHOP is no better than three-weekly, and upfront high-dose therapy with autograft gives no survival gain.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association, HemaSphere, 'Large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL): EHA Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12456099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In advanced disease, radiotherapy is only for a single PET-positive residual site;** PET-negative patients do not routinely need it. (II, B)
claims.locator: European Hematology Association, HemaSphere, 'Large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL): EHA Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12456099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider primary G-CSF and antimicrobial prophylaxis for all curative chemo-immunotherapy,** especially in patients over 60 or on more intensive regimens. Calcium channel blockers may blunt anti-CD20 antibodies, so consider switching them.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association, HemaSphere, 'Large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL): EHA Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12456099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **High CNS relapse risk:** CNS-IPI 4–6 (10–12% risk), two or more extranodal sites, or testis, breast, epidural, orbit, kidney or adrenal involvement. Get MRI and CSF (cytology and flow cytometry) as early as possible, ideally before cycle 1. (III, A)
claims.locator: European Hematology Association, HemaSphere, 'Large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL): EHA Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12456099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **CNS prophylaxis: intrathecal methotrexate is not recommended.** Two cycles of high-dose IV methotrexate (at least 3 g/m²) may be considered (III, B) for high-risk patients who reach complete metabolic response with Pola-R-CHP or R-CHOP.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association, HemaSphere, 'Large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL): EHA Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12456099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Double- or triple-hit lymphoma:** consider an intensive regimen (R-CODOX-M/R-IVAC, DA-EPOCH-R, R-ACVBP or R-CHOEP14) for selected patients (III, B); keep R-CHOP21 for the unfit. Pola-R-CHP does not seem better than R-CHOP here, and autograft consolidation is not recommended.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association, HemaSphere, 'Large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL): EHA Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12456099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma:** use R-CHOP14 or a more intensive regimen (R-M/VACOP-B, R-ACVBP, DA-EPOCH-R) and avoid R-CHOP21. Skip mediastinal radiotherapy after complete metabolic response; a DS5 result (Deauville) needs salvage therapy.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association, HemaSphere, 'Large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL): EHA Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12456099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Primary testicular lymphoma:** six cycles of R-CHOP, radiotherapy to the other testis (strongly advised) and CNS prophylaxis.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association, HemaSphere, 'Large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL): EHA Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12456099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Age 80 or over, or unfit:** use a geriatric assessment, then R-miniCHOP for six cycles in fit patients (I, B), which reduces doxorubicin to 25 mg/m², cyclophosphamide to 400 mg/m² and vincristine to 1 mg. A corticosteroid prephase, optionally with one 1 mg IV dose of vincristine, improves performance status.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association, HemaSphere, 'Large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL): EHA Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12456099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Heart failure or LVEF below 50%: use a regimen without conventional doxorubicin** (R-CEOP, R-GCVP, R-COMP with non-pegylated liposomal doxorubicin, or R-GEMOX). After earlier anthracycline, work within the 450 mg/m² lifetime limit.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association, HemaSphere, 'Large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL): EHA Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12456099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Biopsy before second-line treatment** (III, B), to confirm relapse, exclude another diagnosis and check CD19 and CD20 expression; biopsy again before third line because target antigen can be lost.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association, HemaSphere, 'Large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL): EHA Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12456099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Refractory disease or relapse within 12 months: offer CAR T-cells (axi-cel or liso-cel).** (I, A) Axi-cel improved 4-year overall survival (55% vs 46%). CAR T-cells may not suit patients with performance status 2 or worse, a large tumour burden or fast-rising LDH.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association, HemaSphere, 'Large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL): EHA Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12456099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Relapse more than 1 year after first-line therapy in a fit patient: salvage immunochemotherapy** (R-DHAX, R-ICE, R-GDP or R-ESHAP), then high-dose therapy (such as BEAM) and autograft if chemosensitive (I, B). Long-term PFS is about 40% in late relapse but under 15–20% in early relapse or primary refractory disease.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association, HemaSphere, 'Large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL): EHA Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12456099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Not a candidate for CAR T-cells or transplant: R-GemOx or Pola-BR** (III, B); consider glofitamab with GemOx (I, A), which improved median OS (25.5 vs 12.9 months) over R-GemOx, or tafasitamab-lenalidomide if the disease is not refractory.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association, HemaSphere, 'Large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL): EHA Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12456099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Bendamustine may weaken T-cell fitness** and so reduce the effect of later bispecific antibodies (epcoritamab, glofitamab, odronextamab).
claims.locator: European Hematology Association, HemaSphere, 'Large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL): EHA Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12456099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Third line and beyond:** if CAR T-cells were not used in second line, offer them (III, A); if already CAR T-exposed, offer a CD20xCD3 bispecific (epcoritamab, glofitamab, odronextamab), loncastuximab tesirine, tafasitamab-lenalidomide or immunochemotherapy, and consider a trial.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association, HemaSphere, 'Large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL): EHA Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12456099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do not scan asymptomatic patients routinely** (3B). Review history, examination and blood count for at least 2 years. Being event-free at 2 years means survival matches the general population, and 5 relapse-free years means cure.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association, HemaSphere, 'Large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL): EHA Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12456099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Late effects:** cardiology review and echocardiography within 1 year of finishing, then at 3 and 5 years and every 5 years; breast screening from 8 years after mediastinal radiotherapy; TSH at 1, 2 and 5 years after neck radiotherapy.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association, HemaSphere, 'Large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL): EHA Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 23 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12456099/, retrieved 2026-09-23
